title: What the Apostles Left Behind
english: …good judgment of the apostles. For they left what they had; the livelihood they had, this they disregarded. Their nets were their whole treasure and their whole wealth, for their living lay in their dragnets; the catch of fish fed their hopes of life. Yet they left even these. They did not say to themselves: 'This man tells us nonsense and idle tales; he promises to make us fishers of men (Matthew 4:19). Where is there such a net? Where is a dragnet able to catch such a prey? What lake, what sea will bring men to our nets? What profit will the catch bring? Where shall we use the catch once it is caught?' But heeding the one who called them, made firm by faith, and…
translator_notes: The section opens mid-sentence, completing 'It is fitting, then, to call blessed the good judgment of the apostles.'
'Good judgment' renders εὐγνωμοσύνη, which can also mean 'gratitude'. Here the praise is for the apostles' sound sense in leaving their nets at Christ's call.
'They did not say to themselves' governs all the questions that follow: these are the doubts the apostles did not voice.
The section ends mid-sentence; the next section continues '…perceiving that his word held some hidden meaning, they followed him'.
